chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, who said:

Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was asked about the woman who has a husband, and his intellect has been afflicted after he married her, or insanity has befallen him. So he (peace be upon him) said to her: 'You may remove yourself from him if you wish.'

key_terms.أَبُو إِبْرِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), referring to the 7th Imam Musa al-Kazim
key_terms.تَنْزِعَ نَفْسَهَا: to remove herself (from the marriage bond)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a wife if her husband becomes insane after marriage?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the wife's unilateral right to dissolve the marriage (*tanzi' nafsaha*) if her husband loses his sanity post-nuptials, reflecting the Shia principle of preserving the spouse's well-being when the core element of rational companionship is lost. This ruling underscores the legal significance of *'aql* (intellect/reason) as a fundamental pillar of marital validity and continuity in Shia jurisprudence.
